subject: Startups
title: IBM: Hardware to Services
description: Learn IBM: Hardware to Services in one minute.

hook.text: In 1993, IBM was losing $8 billion a year selling hardware. Lou Gerstner arrived and changed everything.

buildup.text: The board wanted to break IBM into pieces. Gerstner saw that customers needed integrated solutions, not just boxes.

discovery.text: He pivoted IBM from a hardware company to a services and consulting giant. Technology became a means, not the product.

twist.text: IBM eventually sold its PC division to Lenovo in 2005. The company that made the PC walked away from PCs.

climax.text: IBM's services pivot saved the company. It transformed from a dying hardware maker to a $100 billion consultancy.

punchline.text: IBM stopped selling boxes and started selling brains.

quiz.question: What did Lou Gerstner pivot IBM toward?
